name: pipe-stand-trip
title: Pipe Stand Trip
description: A rig-floor progress indicator that racks pipe stands the way a drilling crew actually trips them — elevator down empty, hoist a stand clear, swing it to the fingerboard, rack it, return — the fingerboard filling one slot at a time as the depth counter falls, then unracking in reverse and looping forever.
useWhen: a bounded-but-cyclic progress surface where N discrete units are pulled off a queue and racked one at a time, and the mechanism itself (a physical hoist/swing/rack cycle with a growing fingerboard row) should carry the read rather than an abstract bar or dot; pick queue-triage-ratchet instead when the unit is a card needing an explicit keep/archive decision with undo, or stepper-ratchet when the surface is a bounded numeric input the user directly increments/decrements rather than an ambient, self-driven count.
instruction: A card-scale rig-floor progress indicator built entirely from a single fixed SVG viewBox (0 0 120 150) and preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet", which does the 'derive geometry from the container's smaller dimension' work for free — a narrow card scales the whole derrick down uniformly, never crops it, with no ResizeObserver or JS geometry recompute needed. The derrick is two vertical legs with four horizontal braces and diagonal cross-bracing between them (all --border, strokeOpacity ~0.85, static), a fingerboard bar along the top edge holding 12 evenly-spaced slot rects, a floor line at the bottom (rotary table), and a thin center rail down which a single elevator group (a small rect, --foreground) travels. Motion is five chained CSS transitions on that one <g> ref — style.transform + style.transition set imperatively, no React state and no rAF on the animation hot path — run back-to-back via a recursive setTimeout chain: down-stroke (700ms, ease-in cubic-bezier(0.55,0,1,0.45), empty, rail-top to rotary-table — 'gravity-assisted lowering') -> hoist-up (500ms, ease-out cubic-bezier(0,0.55,0.45,1), rotary-table back to rail-top, a stand rect fades in above the elevator block over 120ms as it attaches — 'block brake sets') -> swing-to-rack (200ms, lateral only, rail-top to the target slot's x) -> rack-seat (300ms, cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1) — a spring/back-out curve that overshoots into the slot and settles, expressing the spec's '~15px overshoot' as viewBox units so it scales with the card; the carried-stand rect fades out the instant this phase ends, the same instant the racked count increments) -> return-down (700ms, ease-in-out, slot back to rail-top, empty). That is exactly 2400ms per stand. Tripping in reverses the same five waypoints in reverse order with custody flipped — swing-in (700ms) -> unseat (300ms, spring, the racked count decrements and the stand-rect fades in at the START of this phase, i.e. the instant of grabbing) -> swing-out (200ms) -> lower-stand (500ms, ease-in, stand-rect fades out at the end — stabbed into the string) -> rise-empty (700ms) — unracking the MOST recently racked slot first (LIFO), which is mechanically correct for running pipe back in. `racked` (0..12) is the one piece of React state that actually matters: it drives BOTH the fingerboard fill (slot i is filled, --ns-muted, iff i < racked) AND the depth counter (displayed as `${12 - racked} STANDS`, or 'OUT' at racked === 12) from the same integer, mutated only at the exact instant custody changes hands, so the two visuals can never desync the way a pair of independently-advanced counters could. Reaching racked === 12 while tripping out holds the elevator at rail-top, empty, label 'OUT', for 1800ms, then flips direction and begins tripping in immediately from racked = 12 (no discontinuous reset). A full loop is 12 stands out (28.8s) + the 1.8s hold + 12 stands in (28.8s) ≈ 59.4s, matching the spec's ~60s figure. On mount the component starts already mid-cycle rather than from an empty derrick — 5 of 12 slots racked, the elevator mid-hoist-up carrying a stand, counter reading '7 STANDS' — per the spec's own worked t0 example, so the very first frame already reads as alive. The one thing to follow: the elevator's current phase (its position along the rail vs. over a slot) together with the fingerboard fill count, at a cadence of one full stand cycle every 2.4s (five sub-phase transitions of 200-700ms each) — comfortably clear of the 'roughly a second between followable events' floor. `prefers-reduced-motion` skips the timer chain entirely and renders one static frame: 5 slots racked, elevator seated at the 5th slot (rack-seat's end position), stand released — 'stand fully racked, elevator still adjacent, mid-settle', the frame that shows the hoist/stand/fingerboard relationship most clearly, chosen over any ambiguous empty-elevator travel frame. Pauses (no timer advanced, no mid-flight element left dangling — an in-flight phase is fast-forwarded to its end state) on IntersectionObserver non-intersection and on `visibilitychange` hidden, resuming from the next phase when visible again. Pure DOM + SVG + CSS, zero canvas, zero dependencies, every color a literal `var(--token)` SVG attribute (--border for static rig structure and empty-slot outlines, --ns-muted for a racked stand, --foreground for the elevator and whatever it is currently carrying) — nothing is read via getComputedStyle because nothing is computed in JS, so there is no first-paint color race to guard against.
